title: Normalized reverse two-point inequality
statement: Let $0<q<p<1$, let $\rho,a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and $|a|<1$. On the one-dimensional Boolean cube, define $f(x)=1+a\sigma(x)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign encoding. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, with the extended power means taken under the uniform measure.
replaced: Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and $|a|<1$. For $f(t)=1+a(-1)^t$ on $\{0,1\}$, $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
